questions.questionText: A shop recorded 12,450 items in stock. It sold 375 items on Monday and 400 on Tuesday. Calculate the number of items remaining. Show all working.
questions.explanation: Subtract both daily sales from the opening stock.

questions.questionText: A farmer used 2/5 of a field for maize and 1/5 for beans. What fraction of the field was used altogether? Give your answer in simplest form and show working.
questions.explanation: Add fractions with the same denominator and simplify.

questions.questionText: A family buys 5 items at $17 each. A 10% discount is given on the total bill. Calculate (a) the total before discount and (b) the amount paid after discount.
questions.explanation: Find quantity × price, calculate 10%, then subtract.

questions.questionText: A rectangular garden measures 15 m by 10 m. Calculate (a) its perimeter and (b) its area. State the correct units.
questions.explanation: Use P=2(l+w) and A=l×w.

questions.questionText: A bus leaves at 11:28 and travels for 2 hours 35 minutes. What time does it arrive? Show how you handle the minutes and hours.
questions.explanation: Add the duration carefully and convert excess minutes to an hour.

questions.questionText: Share $72 in the ratio 3:3. Calculate each person's share and show your method.
questions.explanation: Find total parts, then the value of one part.

questions.questionText: Calculate 5% of $260. Then state the amount remaining after that percentage is deducted.
questions.explanation: Percentage = pct/100 × amount.

questions.questionText: One angle on a straight line is 42°. Calculate the other angle and explain the angle rule you used.
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line total 180°.

questions.questionText: A classroom floor is 28 m long and 16 m wide. Tiles cover 1 m² each. How many tiles are needed to cover the floor, ignoring wastage?
questions.explanation: Calculate the area in square metres.

questions.questionText: A rectangular box is 6 cm long, 7 cm wide and 7 cm high. Calculate its volume in cm³.
questions.explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 6 cm × 7 cm × 7 cm = 294 cm³ [3 marks].

questions.questionText: The numbers of books read by five learners are 12, 18, 20, 24, 26. Calculate (a) the total, (b) the mean, and (c) the range.
questions.explanation: Mean=total÷5; range=highest−lowest.

questions.questionText: A table shows maize sales for three days: Monday 51 kg, Tuesday 66 kg, Wednesday 46 kg. Draw a suitable bar graph and state which day had the highest sales.
questions.explanation: Use a consistent scale and labelled axes.

questions.questionText: A school has $156 for a project. Materials cost $17 each. If the school buys 5 materials, how much money remains? Show working and check whether the budget is sufficient.
questions.explanation: Calculate 5×unit cost and subtract from the budget.

questions.questionText: Consider the pattern 4, 8, 12, 16, ... (a) Write the next three terms. (b) Describe the rule. (c) Find the 10th term.
questions.explanation: The common difference is 4.

questions.questionText: Rudo had $250. She spent 2/5 of it on school uniforms and 20% of the remainder on stationery. How much money did she have left? [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Uniforms = 2/5 × $250 = $100 [1 mark]. Remainder = $250 - $100 = $150 [1 mark]. Stationery = 20% of $150 = $30 [1 mark]. Money left = $150 - $30 = $120 [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A rectangular water tank measures 2.5 m long, 1.2 m wide, and 1.5 m deep. (a) Calculate the volume in m³ [2 marks]. (b) How many litres of water does it hold when full? (1 m³ = 1,000 litres) [2 marks].
questions.explanation:
(a) Volume = 2.5 × 1.2 × 1.5 = 4.5 m³ [2 marks].
(b) Capacity = 4.5 × 1,000 = 4,500 litres [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A farmer borrows $1,200 from a bank at 8% per annum simple interest for 2½ years. Calculate the total amount he must repay at the end of 2½ years. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: SI = (P × R × T) / 100 = (1,200 × 8 × 2.5) / 100 = $240 [2 marks]. Total repayment = Principal + Interest = $1,200 + $240 = $1,440 [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A bus leaves Mutare at 07:35 and reaches Harare at 11:20 after stopping for 25 minutes in Rusape. (a) Find the total time taken [2 marks]. (b) If the distance is 263 km, calculate the average driving speed while moving [3 marks].
questions.explanation:
(a) Total time from 07:35 to 11:20 = 3 hours 45 minutes [2 marks].
(b) Driving time = 3 h 45 min - 25 min = 3 hours 20 minutes = 3⅓ hours (10/3 h) [1 mark]. Speed = 263 ÷ (10/3) = 78.9 km/h [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Share 720 kg of seed among three villages A, B, and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Calculate how many kilograms each village receives. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Total parts = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 [1 mark]. 1 part = 720 ÷ 9 = 80 kg [1 mark]. Village A = 2 × 80 = 160 kg; Village B = 3 × 80 = 240 kg; Village C = 4 × 80 = 320 kg [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A shop sells a television marked at $480 at a 12½% cash discount. Calculate (a) the discount in dollars [2 marks] and (b) the cash price paid by a customer [2 marks].
questions.explanation:
(a) 12½% = 1/8. Discount = $480 ÷ 8 = $60 [2 marks].
(b) Cash price = $480 - $60 = $420 [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Five learners scored 68%, 74%, 82%, 70%, and 86% in a Mathematics test. Find (a) their mean score [2 marks] and (b) the range of the scores [2 marks].
Calculate the perimeter and area of a right-angled triangle whose shorter sides are 6 cm and 8 cm, and whose hypotenuse is 10 cm. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 6 + 8 + 10 = 24 cm [2 marks]. Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm² [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A rectangular school hall floor is 18 m long and 12 m wide. Square tiles of side 50 cm (0.5 m) are used to tile the floor. (a) Calculate the area of the hall floor in m² [2 marks]. (b) How many tiles are needed to cover the whole floor? [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Area of hall = 18 m × 12 m = 216 m² [2 marks].
(b) Area of 1 tile = 0.5 m × 0.5 m = 0.25 m² [1 mark]. Number of tiles = 216 ÷ 0.25 = 864 tiles [2 marks].

questions.questionText: In an election at a primary school, 360 pupils voted. Candidate A received 45% of the votes, Candidate B received 1/3 of the votes, and Candidate C received the rest. How many votes did each candidate receive? [5 marks]
questions.explanation:
Candidate A = 45/100 × 360 = 162 votes [2 marks].
Candidate B = 1/3 × 360 = 120 votes [1 mark].
Candidate C = 360 - (162 + 120) = 78 votes [2 marks].

questions.questionText: A cylindrical drum has a diameter of 14 cm and a height of 20 cm. Taking π = 22/7, calculate the volume of the drum. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Radius r = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm [1 mark]. Volume = πr²h = (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 20 [1 mark] = 22 × 7 × 20 = 3,080 cm³ [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Mrs Moyo buys 3 dozen exercise books at $4.20 per dozen and 8 pens at $0.45 each. She pays with a $20 note. Calculate her change. [4 marks]
